## Capture a saved session

[`capture`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#capture)
reads finished turns from Ramabana’s history file. It does not watch a
running agent. It writes one session as an Aidialog notebook that Leela
can open. The notebook starts with a review note that is skipped when
the dialog is replayed, and its metadata holds the session id, the
model, the route score and the findings, with `status` set to `review`.

All of Dhrona’s notebooks keep their review record under one metadata
key, `REVIEW_KEY`.
[`read_dialog`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#read_dialog)
reads a notebook, and
[`clean_dialog`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#clean_dialog)
returns only its prompt messages, without the review note.

``` python

```

*The newest session id in `turns`.*

``` python
import tempfile
capture_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
history = capture_dir/'history.jsonl'
turn = {
    'session': 'agent_example', 'prompt': 'Use FOSSICK to research a GitHub repository.',
    'reply': 'The repository says demonstrations improve tool use.',
    'activity': [{'id': 'a1', 'tool': 'web_search', 'args': {'query': 'repo'}, 'detail': 'generic result', 'ok': True}],}
history.write_text(json.dumps(turn) + '\n')
review = capture(capture_dir/'github.ipynb', history=history)
dlg = read_dialog(review)
assert dlg.meta[REVIEW_KEY]['status'] == 'review'
assert dlg[0].skipped and dlg[1].msg_type == sprompt
review
```

    Path('/tmp/tmpjoya32yi/github.ipynb')

A tool call without an id gets one made from its turn and position, so
the ids stay unique across the turns of a session.

``` python
noid = [{'session': 'noid', 'prompt': p, 'activity': [{'tool': 'ls', 'args': {}, 'ok': True}]} for p in ('a', 'b')]
history.write_text(json.dumps(turn) + '\n' + ''.join(json.dumps(t) + '\n' for t in noid))
ids = [p.id for m in dlg2chat(clean_dialog(capture(capture_dir/'noid.ipynb', history=history)), plain=True) for p in m.content if isinstance(p, ToolUse)]
assert len(ids) == 2 and len(set(ids)) == 2
history.write_text(json.dumps(turn) + '\n')
```

## Accept a reviewed round

Accepting is a deliberate step.
[`accept`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#accept) checks
that the dialog still converts to chat history and starts with a user
turn, then records the reviewer, the source session, the package version
and the round revision in the notebook’s metadata. It writes the round’s
history as JSON beside the notebook, or at `output`.

### compiled_history

``` python
def compiled_history(
    source
):
```

*The chat history of an accepted round, in Aidialog’s format.*

``` python
compiled = accept(review, reviewer='Karthik')
accepted = compiled.read_json()
assert accepted['meta']['status'] == 'accepted'
history2 = compiled_history(review)
assert history2[0].role == 'user'
assert any(isinstance(p, ToolUse) for m in history2 for p in m.content)
compiled
```

An accepted round also records the tools it calls and the model of its
session, so a warm start can check it against the tools on offer.
`install` copies the JSON into the rounds library through
[`install_round`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#install_round).
[`accept`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#accept) still
returns the path of the JSON it wrote. To get the library path, call
`install_round(out, into=...)` yourself, which is safe to repeat, or
look in `ROUNDS_DIR/f'{name}.json'`.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    lib = Path(d)/'lib'
    out = accept(review, reviewer='Karthik', output=Path(d)/'r.json', install=lib)
    meta = out.read_json()['meta']
    assert meta['tools'] == ['web_search'] and 'model' in meta and meta['name'] == 'github'
    assert (lib/'github.json').read_json() == out.read_json()
    again = install_round(out, into=lib)   # the helper `accept(install=)` uses; call it to learn the library path
    assert again == lib/'github.json' and again.read_json() == out.read_json()
    assert install_round(out, into=Path(d)/'other', name='mine') == Path(d)/'other'/'mine.json'
```

The dialog helpers keep a review note through a save and a load, and
[`read_dialog`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#read_dialog)
refuses a notebook it cannot read.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    dlg = Dialog([], name='t')
    dlg.mk_message('hi', msg_type=sprompt)
    p = _write_dlg(dlg, Path(d)/'sub/t.ipynb')
    _add_review(dlg, {'status': 'review'}, 'note'); _write_dlg(dlg, p)
    c = clean_dialog(p)
    assert len(c) == 1 and c[0].msg_type == sprompt and read_dialog(p).meta[REVIEW_KEY]['status'] == 'review'
    try: read_dialog(Path(d)/'missing.ipynb'); assert False
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError): pass
```

    /tmp/tmpuoeet23s/missing.ipynb does not exist

## Start a Ramabana session

Ramabana has no command-line option for loading prepared history.
[`start_round`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#start_round)
therefore sends the accepted round as a first prompt, written by
[`bootstrap_prompt`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#bootstrap_prompt),
which ends by asking for the reply `DHRONA_READY`. Ramabana saves that
turn, and a second command resumes the same session for normal work.
Without `launch`,
[`start_round`](https://Karthik777.github.io/drona/rounds.html#start_round)
returns the two commands instead of running them.

## Command line

Capture, acceptance and launch are separate commands: `dhrona-capture`,
`dhrona-accept` and `dhrona-start`. `dhrona-start` prints the commands
it would run unless `--launch` is set.
